items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters with 91 story missions in total, following the duo Jason and Lucia through Leonida's criminal underworld.
Story missions per chapter are 22, 11, 26, 25 and 7. Chapter 2 also has three optional missions and Chapter 3 has one.
The chapters are named Just Like Paradise, Paradise Lost, Tits Ass Drug Money, Vice City Baby, and Top of the World, Ma. They are set mainly in the Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, and then Vice City.

Each chapter has a point of no return. For example, Chapter 1 locks once you start Tourist Trap, and Chapter 3 ends after the Cartel Heist, where you pick Hang Out or Go Now. After the finale you return to the Chapter 5 point of no return to finish side content.

The two playable leads are Jason and Lucia. Chapter 1 starts with Jason, and Lucia joins in after her prologue and the Coming Home mission. Supporting names include Donnie, Cal, Dre'Quan, Raul, Tyrone, and Boobie.
Leonida has six regions: Vice City, Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park. Rockstar says the map is about twice the size of GTA 5's.
One interactive map lists 1,075 marked places across Leonida, sorted into nine categories. Those include robbery targets, safehouses, and hidden packages.
There are 18 collectible card sets. Cards can be sold at pawn shops, and you can view your collection in a wooden box in your apartment.
Dexerto has pinned 103 collectible cards on its map so far, spread across places like Hamlet, Key Lento, Port Gellhorn, and Grassrivers.
Cards, books and magazines found in safehouses like the Chapter 2 motel move elsewhere after a chapter's point of no return. You can still find them, but not in the original spot.

Optional Chapter 2 activities include Thrillbillies, Twist Wrist Smash Grab, Hit Kingpin Bowling, Hit Avery Pawn, and Veteran Hunted, which is Jason only. You can do them before leaving the motel area.

The side content includes Strangers & Freaks missions, such as Kirk's skunk ape hunt, plus robbery missions like Moses vehicle drop-offs and Kitty Litter Labs. There is also a house repair exploration task.
Money is tight early on, and robbery loot is sold in stash bags to fences, Tyrone in Vice City, or earlier contacts like Donnie and Dunk. Tyrone pays the best prices.
Chapter 4's Bad Driver mission lets you kill Felipe for an immediate $20,000. Sparing him instead unlocks his car later.
Vans have 10 slots for stash bags, which is why they suit loot runs. Pest control vans are parked outside the Hamlet warehouse.
A Chapter 3 Snapmatic post leads to a free garage and a unique 1010 Cheetah. The post disappears after a while, so check your phone often.
Make manual saves often and rotate save slots. Missions can't be replayed, and old manual saves are the only way to redo story sections without restarting.
Before ditching Donnie's car in Chapter 1, take the unique H&L .38 Revolver from its trunk. You can't get it once the car is gone.
Update 1.002.002 came out on November 23. It fixes crashes, autosave failures, weather that wouldn't change, phone calls that failed to trigger, and the inability to lose a Wanted level.
The patch also fixed a stuck gym deadlift bar and partners not handing over bags to sell to fences.

A Chapter 3 softlock is still reported after the patch. After the Missing Persons side quest, Jason is greyed out and can't be selected. Reported workarounds are loading an older manual save or calling Dunk.
The base game is 212GB, and PS5 players were still reporting error CE-108255-1 as of November 25. Free space of about twice the install size may be needed to install patches.
